title: MDLoader: A Hybrid Model-Driven Data Loader for Distributed Graph Neural Network Training
problem: Determining optimal communication strategy for distributed data fetching in GNN training on HPC systems, where performance depends on dataset characteristics, training scale, and network topology. The choice between one-sided and collective communication requires dynamic adaptation.
motivation: Scalable in-memory distributed data management with rapid random access is essential for distributed deep learning on HPC platforms to support stochastic optimizers processing large scientific datasets.
method: MDLoader automatically chooses the best communication strategy for moving data across computers during neural network training, using Tree of Parzen Estimators (a technique that efficiently predicts which strategies work best under different conditions) to decide at training startup. The system learned that collective communication—sending identical messages to all computers—works best with large mini-batches and few computers, while one-sided communication—sending targeted messages to specific computers—is faster at larger scales. It picks whichever strategy fits your configuration.
key_novelty: MDLoader dynamically selects between one-sided and collective communication using Tree of Parzen Estimators to predict which strategy will be fastest.
contributions: Hybrid in-memory data loader that dynamically selects between one-sided and collective communication strategies
Model-driven performance estimator using Tree of Parzen Estimators for predicting optimal communication method
Empirical analysis showing communication strategy effectiveness varies with mini-batch size, process count, and training scale
Evaluation on NERSC Perlmutter and OLCF Summit demonstrating 2.83× speedup with 94-96% prediction accuracy

metrics.other: 96.3% prediction success rate (Perlmutter), 94.3% prediction success rate (Summit)

primary_theme: Adaptive communication strategy selection for distributed GNN data loading
